newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere seeks Dasa space JV by November.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere seeks Dasa space JV by November.

text.p: French conglomerate Lagardere hopes to complete a valuation process with Daimler Benz Aerospace (Dasa) that will allow them to set up a space joint venture by November, an MMS executive said on Tuesday.

Patrick Jordan, director of marketing and strategy for Matra Marconi Space (MMS), said the MMS shareholders had signed firm agreements with Dasa to define the due diligence process which will value Dasa's Dornier space business and MMS.
MMS is a joint venture between Lagardere and General Electric Co Plc (GEC).
Jordan was speaking to reporters at MMS UK Ltd's headquarters in Stevenage, southeast England.
The valuation takes into account the assets, including order books, and their five-year business plans, he said.

Based on initial information, MMS' value far exceeded Dasa's and indicated that MMS will hold above 50 percent and between 60-70 percent of the new Anglo-French and German venture. Dasa will hold the rest of the capital.

MMS chairman and chief executive Armand Carlier will be nominated as CEO for the new venture, which will have two Germans and a British executive on the four-man board. Voting will be split 50-50 between MMS and Dasa despite the difference in stakes.
MMS had 1996 sales of 8.4 billion francs but this will rise to 15 billion francs when Dasa joins the group.

Jordan said Dasa's decision to join the MMS group was based on industrial logic and followed MMS' presentation of its business plan. Strong growth in the commercial satellite market demanded Dasa join or be left out, and also to confront the threat of U.S. giants such as Hughes and Lockheed Martin .
"If Europe remains in pieces or Balkanised, we will not stand a chance. We have to, at any cost, increase in size," Carlier said.

Lagardere's agreement with Dasa, announced with its offer in the privatisation of French defence electronics firm Thomson- CSF , has sparked outrage at state-owned Aerospatiale which has been trying to form missiles and space ventures with Dasa, its long-time partner and senior partner in Airbus Industrie.
